value: Basemaps (2026-11-27): the site is built with the long-term unrestricted LINZ Basemaps key LINZ issued for the GitHub Pages site (replaced the 90-day individual key). Every web build/pages deploy must pass LINZ_BASEMAPS_KEY or Topographic and Aerial (LINZ) disappear. The key is public by design: read it from the deployed gh-pages index.html (basemapsKey); never commit it. It is not the LDS key. LINZ terms: show 'LINZ CC BY 4.0' attribution (the map shows 'LINZ Basemaps CC BY 4.0'); no bulk caching of tiles (if ever cached for offline use: about 10 tiles/s and < 250,000 tiles per day per user).

Parallel agents on separate branches can mint the same beads id (rf-aq6.21 collided 2026-11-18: the merge kept the ML agent's). After any merge from main, run bd import .beads/issues.jsonl BEFORE creating or exporting issues, or the export overwrites the other agent's record.

Container is ephemeral: beads Dolt DB is not in git. .beads/issues.jsonl is auto-exported by the pre-commit hook; memories go in .beads/memories.jsonl (see CLAUDE.md). Restore in a fresh clone: bd init --prefix rf --non-interactive, then bd import both files.
Core algorithm choice: own numba Priority-Flood (Barnes 2014) + D8 + Kahn topological-sort accumulation; cross-check vs RichDEM/pysheds. Validate vs NIWA REC2 CATCHAREA.

DEMs come from public s3://nz-elevation COG+STAC (EPSG:2193, NZVD2016). Use dem_8m (new-zealand/new-zealand-contour/dem_8m) for catchment area, 1m LiDAR (bay-of-plenty_2019-2022, waikato_2021, northland_2018-2020) for gradients. Never route flow on DSM.

External data (2026-11-18): OSM waterfalls/rapids/roads/tracks come from Overture Maps GeoParquet on public S3 (overturemaps-us-west-2, release 2026-10-21.0, anonymous pyarrow + bbox filter) because Geofabrik/Overpass/LINZ are blocked or reset at the egress. river-finder external fetch|attach -> data/nz/{waterfalls,access}.gpkg, external.pkl (national_table order), viewer <region>_x.txt (3x u16 dist/10 m + u8 falls_n + u8 max h) and <region>_falls.json. ODbL attribution.

LDS: Sean's LINZ Data Service key works (confirmed 2026-11-18); pass it only as env LINZ_LDS_KEY for a command (sent as Authorization: key header by linz.py); never write it to files, commits, memories or pages. It is NOT a Basemaps key (Basemaps rejects it).

1 m LiDAR rebuild decisions (Sean, 2026-11-26/27): route at 2 m from the full-resolution 1 m block mean (~200 tiles of ~32 km + 3 km halo); sample profiles/sections at 1 m; LiDAR reach geometry, LINZ lines for names only; reach areas from network accumulation; reference areas folded in (one comparison against the old outputs, then retire the per-region pipeline); national 1 m mosaic only; no DSM/canopy read; train card v5 on the 1 m data, archive v1-v4; build into data/nz1m/ then switch. Spec: docs/lidar-extraction-spec.md. No national run until rf-lxa children are done and the user confirms.

ML evaluation (2026-11-18): river-finder ml table|explore|cv|page (~10 min after nz scan). Headline style-matched AUC (MB1997 Track B, slope+confinement) does not control size; style x size AUC separates models (flow 0.68, logit 0.75-0.77, LightGBM 0.79-0.80). OSM falls/rapids and karst bed add ~0; coordinates overfit (LORO drops). Results models/cv/results.json; page data/viewer_nz/ml.html, published as ml.html on the viewer artifact.

Model registry (2026-11-13): models/*.json frozen cards (baseline-flow, v1 checkpoint, v2, v2-published), models/splits/guides-v1.json (river-level, seed 20261113), models/evaluations.json. CLI: river-finder models table|checkpoint|baseline|import|split|train|evaluate|viewer. Viewer score files <region>_m_<model>.txt (u16 pct*100 + u8 flags). Key finding: v1 is at chance on held-out guide rivers (AUC 0.53); flood size alone gets 0.92, so watch size-matched AUC (v2 0.69, baseline 0.55).

National 8 m scan: 115 tiles, 1,104,794 segments (2026-11-13; rebuilt 2026-11-19 with areacode.py for every land cell, ~2 h of tiles + 1 h of steps: score 3 min, export 1, viewer 25, external attach 5, ml table <1, models viewer <1, web data 25). Container/worker restarts kill background jobs: launch with setsid nohup and re-launch; nz tiles resumes (tile.json done flag). Site: 19 regions, 728 MB on Pages; too big for an artifact (256 MB/version), which keeps the 3 reference regions.

Network: session env 'river-finder' allows services3.arcgis.com (REC2), gis.gns.cri.nz, overpass-api.de (OSM), data.mfe.govt.nz, catalogue.data.govt.nz, nz-elevation S3. The LINZ Data Service needs an API key and is not allowed.

Phase 9 findings (2026-11-11): height-to-area (Melton) and height-to-width separate known runs only weakly; regression gives both negative weights after ksn/power. Pareto frontier favours extremes; Mangakarengorengo is #25/90 by Pareto+weighted score but #2/90 by the trained model. riverguide.co.nz markers come from api.riverguide.co.nz GraphQL; scripted access was denied by the classifier, so Sean must decide how to get sections.

Verified via REC2: Tuakopai is spelled 'Tuakopae Stream' in REC2 (outlet 175.984,-37.843, 8.5 km2), inside the Mangakarengorengo River catchment (outlet 176.043,-37.806, 108 km2), which joins the Wairoa (mouth 176.093,-37.686, 464 km2). Bboxes in regions/*.toml come from REC2 upstream traces. Names: NZ_River_Names_REC2_V1 FeatureServer (nzsegment, RivName); geometry/topology: REC2_Layers/0 (HydroID, NextDownID, CUM_AREA in m2).

Reference regions: Kaimai Range (Tuakopai -> Mangakarengorengo -> Wairoa) and Tutamoe/Waima plateau, Northland (Waima, Waipoua?, Mangakahia). Hypothesis: hard volcanic caprock plateau + high rainfall + escarpment incision -> creeks. Bboxes must be checked by us (Sean can't).

River chain (from Sean): Tuakopai -> Mangakarengorengo ('Manga Korekere') -> Wairoa. Wairoa and Tuakopai are in online guides; Mangakarengorengo is NOT (known locally as the flood run). It is the key held-out validation case: the tool must flag it as an unlisted candidate.

Sean's runnability framing (2026-11-11): three main parameters = flow, gradient, height-to-area (prefers) or height-to-width. Start with weighted sum + threshold, later XGBoost/linear model and a Pareto frontier. Known top flood runs: Tuakopai, Mangakarengorengo, Wairoa, Karangahake (K Gorge). Do NOT ask for the LINZ API key via a form.

3D separation viewer added (2026-11-11). Labels in labels/known_runs.toml (status runnable/not_runnable, grade, held_out, extent via put_in/take_out or outlet+upstream_km or whole steep river). First AUCs (runs, all regions): flow 88%, gradient 48%, Melton 14% (inverse).

Built 2026-11-11: river-finder CLI (fetch/route/validate/export/viewer/run). Contour 8 m DEM has flat valley floors between 20 m contours, so flat resolution (Barnes 2014b) is required. River mouths on dune flats are ambiguous; measure named rivers >=500 m inland. Validation: named rivers within 3.2%; >5 km2 within 10%: 70-82% (target 90% not met).

Phases 5-8 done on reference regions (2026-11-11): routing on 5 m LiDAR hybrid; reaches.py segments; scoring.py (run finder, signature, composite, logistic regression). Hold-out: Mangakarengorengo ranks #1/#2 of 47 unlisted Kaimai runs. Hydrology = NIWA Henderson&Collins MAF (MfE rainfall grid blocked). Labels heuristic until Sean gives guide sections.

Sean's preferences: browser viewer first plus a GIS export (GeoPackage + QGIS project). Search scope eventually the whole North Island. Gradient band variable, default 20-80 m/km. Wants a composite overlay, possibly from a simple linear/logistic regression trained on per-point features.

v3 (2026-11-18): models/v3.json kind gbm (LightGBM gbm_terrain recipe, booster models/v3.lgb.txt, sha-checked), trained on guides-v1 like v2; default model. Held-out style x size 0.859 vs v2 0.768 (river-level split flatters GBM; catchment CV 0.804 vs 0.754). Score any frame with models.logits (ml.enrich adds geology/karst/reach type); national from ml_table. Audit: river-finder ml audit (top 1% of UNLISTED reaches; national top 1% is 97% guide reaches).
